intent: Dashboard: a slow listing no longer blocks unrelated requests (threaded server, safe shared state)
notes: Shared Dashboard state is now published as whole snapshots and never changed in place: the registry and the Fleet data are read through `_registry_snapshot()` / `_fleet_snapshot()` and replaced under one writer lock. Registering, removing and changing a repository's config no longer lose updates or alter data that another request is still reading.

Changes to one repository can no longer overlap: register, remove, update, gatorize, config and topology for the same repository run one at a time. A second request gets a clear "another change is running" (409), and a change that arrives after a remove gets 404 instead of acting on a removed repository. Refresh runs one collection at a time and no longer brings back a repository removed while it ran. Audit-session requests are serialized, and a Loop action that times out on a busy loop lock gets a retryable 503 instead of a dropped connection.

Restart and upgrade now wait (up to 5 s) for changes already in progress before the process is replaced, and refuse new ones meanwhile with "dashboard is restarting" (503), so a Loop action or registry write is not cut off half-way. The restart request itself still answers immediately, and repeat requests do not trigger a second restart.

The Dashboard now serves requests concurrently (`DashboardHTTPServer`, at most 16 workers, at most 4 on expensive listing/search/Git work). A slow repository listing no longer makes an unrelated document or click wait behind it: on this repository a small file read stays around 8 ms while four 3-second listings run. A browser test reproduces the old symptom on the single-request server and passes on the new one. This removes one plausible cause of the #70 Windows UI flakes; it is not claimed to close #70.
